column1: # Phiora, which keeps every app's records and every person's own
# documents (puikit: app/phiora-server). The window asks it first for
# Phiogy's own document, as a page does (puikit: loadApp in
# app/phi-kit/src/data.ts), and reads the app's own file where Phiora
# does not answer. With Phiora answering, what a person writes, marks
# and pins is kept there too, as a page keeps it (puikit: persisted in
# Where it is on this machine, for `--local` (else it is on the app's
# server, data/app.tsv); the setting of the system that names another
# place, as the web's VITE_PHI_API does (`localhost:4300`,
# `https://phiegg.com/api`); the word that, given as the place, has
# nobody asked; how long it is waited for at each address its name
# stands for, and how long for its answer once it is reached, in
# milliseconds (one over the internet, at least data/net.tsv's `far`).
# What it is asked by: an app's document ({key} is the app), who the
# one asking is, and one of their own documents ({name} is its name).
# The status of an answer that is one, and of a document that was
# kept; the head that says how long what follows is; the head that says
# it comes in pieces, and its word for that; and the head that gives
# the one asking a session, which is sent back with every ask after.
# What the window calls itself to Phiora, which names a session by it.
# What is asked: the kind of ask, then a line of its head. `get` reads,
# `put` keeps a document, and `post` asks for something to be done.
# {path} is what is asked for, {speak} the protocol, {host} where
# Phiora is, {agent} what the window calls itself, {cookie} the
# session, {length} how long what is sent is.
# patch changes a record and delete takes one away (Phiora's /tree/item).
